The correct structure for a first conditional sentence is: If + present simple, will + base verb.
  • provide (verb (base form)): Base form of the verb. Used for present simple or with modal verbs, but not correct here because the main clause of the first conditional needs 'will + verb'.
  • will provide (verb (future simple)): Future simple tense. Used in the main clause of the first conditional to express what will happen if a certain condition is met.
  • would provide (verb (conditional)): Conditional form (would + base verb). Used in the second conditional for unreal or hypothetical situations, not for real future possibilities.
  • are providing (verb (present continuous)): Present continuous tense. Used for actions happening now or around now, not suitable for this conditional structure.
Related structure or vocabulary: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base verb. Used to talk about real and possible situations in the future.

  • is completed (verb (passive voice)): Present simple passive. Used for general truths or routines, not for future actions.
  • was completed (verb (passive voice)): Past simple passive. Refers to an action finished in the past.
  • will be completed (verb (passive voice)): Future simple passive. Used to describe an action that will be finished in the future.
  • are completed (verb (passive voice)): Present simple passive (plural). Used for general truths or routines, not for future actions.
